newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-ALONSO REACHES FIRST ATP TOUR FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ALONSO REACHES FIRST ATP TOUR FINAL.

text.p: Spain's Julian Alonso reached his first ATP Tour final at only his third attempt when he beat Czech Slava Dosedel at the Generali Open on Saturday.
Alonso, 19, who this week received his lowest-ever world ranking of 92, dominated much of the clay court match which lasted little more than an hour and ended 6-3 6-4.
Earlier this year, Alonso made the third round at Key Biscayne by defeating Steve Bryan and Tim Henman, and the second round in Barcelona.
He also won two challenger tournaments in 1997 in Venice and Contrexville. His entry into the top 100 has given Spain a record 15 players in the category.
"I didn't think I could make it this far, but I improved from match to match and now I think I could even win this tournament," said Alonso.
"I don't care who my next opponent is. When I am on the court I am at war with myself and not my opponent."
His rioval on Sunday will be the winner of the semifinal between compatriot Galo Blanco and 10th-seeded Belgian Filip Dewulf.
Alonso, sponsored and managed by former leading Spanish player Emilio Sanchez, took a quick 5-1 lead in the first set before his form wavered slightly and he dropped serve at 5-2.
But he quickly recuperated, re-broke and took the set on serve before beginning the second set with a break.
Although 15th-seeded Dosedel stepped up a gear and broke for 2-2, he was unable to match Alonso's pace. Dosedel lost his serve at 4-3 and three games later was out.
